_comment_parameters: suggestion.parameter values are config/setup_parameters.json registry keys (WP2b-1). A rule's suggestion is either a single action object or a list of action objects (an atomic package -- e.g. wing+rake -- or an axle-symmetric FL+FR/RL+RR pair, since the registry has no combined axle-level ARB/camber/damper key, see arb_fl notes). Every action is either delta-style {parameter, direction, delta} (delta is SIGNED, in the parameter's native unit/step -- feasibility is current_value + delta against the registry's value_space min/max) or target-style {parameter, target} (a literal value, used only for categorical parameters like abs_position where 'direction' has no meaning -- always feasible, never checked against setup_data). weight moved from suggestion to the rule's own top level in WP2b-2 (a scoring parameter, not a physical-action parameter, and suggestion can now be a list).
_comment_trigger: condition.trigger selects how a rule fires. 'data': fires from classify_fn (verdict + min_severity) on the rule's phases; feedback_sign/min_feedback_abs only modulate the score (agreement_bonus / conflict_penalty / 1.0 if feedback absent). 'driver': fires from feedback_sign/min_feedback_abs on the rule's phases alone (score scales with max |feedback|/5 among those phases); condition.verdict is NOT a firing gate here -- it is only the agreement reference against which classify_fn's verdict on the same phases is compared, to modulate the score (agreement_bonus if it matches, conflict_penalty + the corner listed in conflicts if it contradicts with the opposite axle verdict, 1.0 if data is silent/ok). 'both': fires only when the data condition AND the driver condition both hold independently -- no further modulation, higher default weight (high-confidence tier).
_comment_source_balance: settings.source_balance (0..1) is a global multiplier on top of the per-trigger score, applied after agreement/conflict modulation: data-triggered rules get (1 - source_balance) * 2, driver-triggered rules get source_balance * 2, both-triggered rules always get 1.0 (corroborated evidence is never discounted). Default 0.5 is exactly neutral (both multipliers = 1.0, current behaviour unchanged). At the extremes a single-source rule still fires and evaluates -- its match, corner, and conflict flag still exist -- but its score multiplies to 0 and it drops out at min_score_to_show, which is suppression at the scoring stage only, not at the evaluation stage. source_balance does not touch agreement_bonus/conflict_penalty: balance weighs WHO may raise a hypothesis, modulation weighs WHAT the other source says about it.
_comment_worst_corner: settings.worst_corner_multiplier scales EVERY match's score on a corner the driver flagged as 'worst' in the feedback table, regardless of trigger type -- applied once, after source_balance and agreement/conflict modulation. It is orthogonal to both: source_balance weighs who may raise a hypothesis, agreement/conflict weighs what the other source says about a specific match, worst_corner_multiplier weighs the driver's own prioritisation of which corner matters most this outing. Default 1.5; a corner with no 'worst' flag is unaffected (implicit x1.0). Multiple flagged corners each get the multiplier independently.
_comment_cell_id_status: cell_id is the forward-reference key into the engineer decision matrix (external, maintained outside this repo) that a matrix-derived rule encodes -- document leads code, every matrix cell has exactly one JSON entry, including the two cells the matrix defines no action for (OS-BRK-low, INST-ENT) and the escalation cells not yet activated. status extends seed|reviewed to: elicited (matrix-derived, sourced from the authoritative decision matrix but not yet engineering-reviewed in-tool -- NOT a placeholder guess the way the old ARB-only seeds were), held (escalation rule, fully specified for 1:1 traceability but never fires -- no applied-recommendations history exists yet to know whether the base change was tried, see each held rule's rationale), dropped (matrix cell deliberately defines no action -- recorded, never fires), retired (superseded, kept for history, never fires). generate_recommendations skips any rule whose status is held, dropped, or retired.
_comment_consistency_gate: Global policy (decision matrix): no recommendation unless the triggering verdict repeats across laps for the same stable_corner_id. Evaluated per-lap (not just on the median-of-medians aggregate) for every 'data'/'both'-trigger rule: min_repeat_laps is an absolute floor, min_repeat_fraction is a fraction of that corner's analysed laps -- BOTH must hold (AND, not OR). 'driver'-trigger rules are exempt (driver feedback has no lap dimension, see _feedback_row).
_comment_change_budget: Distinct from max_recommendations (a DISPLAY cap, unchanged -- up to 8 ranked results still render for context). change_budget governs which results get the 'selected' marker: the tool marks the top default_max non-conflicted, feasible results as selected after ranking (severity, corner count, escalation_tier, cell_id -- see modules/recommendation.py ranking), walking further down the ranked list to fill the budget if a higher-ranked result is parameter_conflict or infeasible. absolute_cap is exposed for a future manual engineer override UI; the tool itself never auto-selects past default_max.
_comment_action_class: WP2b-2 amendment 7: a 'data'-trigger match at moderate severity with no driver corroboration on the same phases is ADVISORY (an observation + most likely lever, non-imperative rationale, never budget-eligible) rather than RECOMMENDED -- mild understeer is this car's deliberate stable baseline (June driver-report precedent) and the elicitation's own bias is against unnecessary changes when the driver is inconsistent with the data. A match is RECOMMENDED if its trigger is in always_recommended_triggers (driver/both are already corroborated by construction), or if trigger is 'data' and either severity is in data_trigger_recommended_severities (default: 'strong') or driver feedback on the same phases agrees with the data verdict (corroborated). A bucket is RECOMMENDED if ANY of its matches reach that bar, else ADVISORY -- advisory-only matches still contribute evidence/score, they just cannot carry the bucket to budget-eligible on their own.

rules.name: Entry understeer (data) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Front axle saturating at turn-in (understeer): softening the front ARB lowers front roll-stiffness share, which lowers front lateral load transfer and frees grip on the sliding (front) axle.

rules.name: Exit oversteer / traction (data) -> soften rear ARB
rules.rationale: Rear axle losing grip on power application (oversteer): softening the rear ARB lowers rear roll-stiffness share, which lowers rear lateral load transfer and frees grip on the sliding (rear) axle, restoring traction and stability on exit.

rules.name: Apex understeer (data) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Sustained mid-corner understeer at peak lateral load: softening the front ARB lowers front roll-stiffness share, which lowers front lateral load transfer and frees grip on the sliding (front) axle through the apex.

rules.name: Unstable yaw on entry (data) -> soften rear ARB
rules.rationale: Destabilising yaw moment while trail-braking into the corner (rear-limited rotation): softening the rear ARB lowers rear roll-stiffness share, which lowers rear lateral load transfer and frees grip on the rear axle, adding yaw damping on entry.

rules.name: Driver-reported exit oversteer (driver) -> soften rear ARB
rules.rationale: Driver reports strong oversteer on exit (|feedback| >= 3): softening the rear ARB lowers rear roll-stiffness share, which lowers rear lateral load transfer and frees grip on the sliding (rear) axle. Classifier agreement/conflict on the same phases modulates the score.

rules.name: Driver-reported entry understeer (driver) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Driver reports strong understeer on entry (|feedback| >= 3): softening the front ARB lowers front roll-stiffness share, which lowers front lateral load transfer and frees grip on the sliding (front) axle. Classifier agreement/conflict on the same phases modulates the score.

rules.name: Entry understeer, data + driver agree (both) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Classifier and driver independently confirm entry understeer: softening the front ARB lowers front roll-stiffness share, which lowers front lateral load transfer and frees grip on the sliding (front) axle. High-confidence tier since both sources corroborate.

rules.name: Understeer, braking, low speed -> ABS front-stable map
rules.rationale: Matrix v2 decode (project-lead review, 2026-07-26): the original v1 transmission's ABS-map answer for this cell was garbled and had been defaulted (project-default) to a literal ABS position; decoded, the engineer's actual first change is front toe +0.5mm more toe-out (registry step) -- sharpens turn-in response, directly addressing front-axle understeer risk under braking at low corner speed. The ABS-map idea survives as a held escalation (see US-BRK-low-esc), not the first change.

rules.name: Escalation: US-BRK-low -> ABS try-and-error, FA stability target
rules.rationale: Held escalation for US-BRK-low (matrix v2, project-lead review): if front toe-out alone doesn't resolve it, try-and-error 1-2 ABS positions within the current dry grip-level bracket, targeting the front-axle-stable variant (see car_data.json abs table -- this is an ordinal nudge WITHIN a bracket, not a jump across grip levels; see config/setup_parameters.json abs_position notes, 'superseded-in-practice' annotation). Matrix v2 states a 1-2 position range, not a single value -- 1 chosen as the conservative default per this project's existing convention for stated ranges (cf. the rake package magnitude). Not automated -- held pending an applied-recommendations history log (future WP) that can confirm the base toe change was actually tried before escalating.

rules.name: Understeer, braking, medium speed -> front bump LS softer
rules.rationale: Front-axle understeer under trail-braking, medium corner speed: opening front low-speed bump 3 clicks (both front corners, axle-symmetric per team practice, see damper_bump_ls_fl notes) softens nose-dive control into the corner, reducing front-axle load-transfer rate under trail braking.

rules.name: Escalation: US-BRK-med -> front ARB softer, rear ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Held escalation for US-BRK-med: softening front ARB 2 positions lowers front roll-stiffness share directly (car_data.json arb.front), while stiffening rear ARB 1 position redistributes roll stiffness rearward, jointly freeing front-axle grip under trail-braking if the damper change alone is not enough. Not automated -- held pending an applied-recommendations history log (future WP) that can confirm the base change was actually tried before escalating; promote status to 'elicited' once that WP lands.

rules.name: Understeer, braking, high speed -> wing up + rake forward (package)
rules.rationale: Front-axle understeer under braking at high corner speed, where aero balance dominates: one wing step up (car_data.json wing_position_table) adds rear downforce/stability headroom, and 1mm of forward rake (front ride height down, rear up -- WP2b-2 decision (1)) shifts the aero platform's pressure centre rearward. Both raise braking-phase stability so more front grip stays available for the understeer-limited axle. Applied atomically as one package (one change-budget slot, not two).

rules.name: Escalation: US-BRK-high -> front bump HS softer
rules.rationale: Held escalation for US-BRK-high: opening front high-speed bump 2 clicks adds kerb/bump compliance on top of the wing+rake package, for cases where the aero-platform change alone does not resolve high-speed braking understeer. Not automated -- held pending an applied-recommendations history log (future WP) that can confirm the base change was actually tried before escalating; promote status to 'elicited' once that WP lands.

rules.name: Understeer, turn-in, low speed -> front toe more toe-out
rules.rationale: Front-axle understeer at turn-in, low corner speed: 0.5mm more front toe-out (registry step) sharpens initial turn-in response, directly countering the front-axle-led verdict at this phase.

rules.name: Understeer, turn-in, medium speed -> diff position down
rules.rationale: Front-axle understeer at turn-in, medium speed: one less differential locking-torque position (car_data.json diff_locking_torque.positions) reduces the diff's resistance to axle-speed difference on turn-in trail-throttle, letting the front axle rotate into the corner more freely.

rules.name: Understeer, turn-in, high speed -> wing down
rules.rationale: Front-axle understeer at turn-in, high speed: one wing step down reduces rear downforce, shifting the aero front/rear balance toward relatively more front grip at the speed where aero, not mechanical grip, dominates.

rules.name: Understeer, apex, low speed -> front ARB softer
rules.rationale: Sustained apex understeer, low corner speed, mechanical-grip-dominated: softening front ARB 1 position (both corners) lowers front roll-stiffness share, freeing mid-corner front grip. Alternative lever noted by matrix v2 (project-lead review 2026-07-26): rear ARB +1 (stiffening rear roll-stiffness share indirectly rotates the car more, easing understeer) -- this rule keeps front ARB soften as its primary, action-eligible lever; the rear-ARB alternative is not separately encoded.

rules.name: Understeer, apex, medium speed -> diff position down
rules.rationale: Apex understeer, medium speed, under partial throttle: one less diff locking-torque position reduces power-on axle-speed resistance through the apex, easing the understeer a locked diff can induce.

rules.name: Escalation: US-APX-med -> TC LAT up (power-understeer)
rules.rationale: Held escalation, power-understeer rationale (thesis_notes.md, 'TC LAT for power-induced understeer - engineer rationale resolved' [2026-07-25]): raising TC LAT one position (car_data.json tc table) cuts torque sooner under lateral load, reducing acceleration squat and keeping load on the front axle -- 'more reserves on the front' for a pushing car under power, not the anti-rotation effect the LAT convention describes for an oversteering car. Scoping caveat from that same note: valid for understeer WITH throttle involvement (apex-on-power, exit), not off-throttle push -- this rule does not yet scope on throttle/ax, so promoting it out of 'held' should add that check. Not automated -- held pending an applied-recommendations history log (future WP) that can confirm the base change was actually tried before escalating; promote status to 'elicited' once that WP lands.

rules.name: Understeer, apex, high speed -> front camber more negative
rules.rationale: Apex understeer, high corner speed, sustained peak lateral load: 0.1deg more front negative camber (registry step, corrected 2026-07-26 project-lead review -- see config/setup_parameters.json camber_fl/fr notes) increases the front contact patch's effective camber gain under load, adding peak front lateral grip at the load level high-speed apex understeer occurs at. Typical field practice is a 0.2deg change (two 0.1deg clicks); confirm tyre surface/wear pattern before applying camber changes. A one-sided (single-corner, FL or FR only) change is sometimes preferred over this rule's symmetric FL+FR pair -- engineer's call, not encoded here.

rules.name: Understeer, exit, low speed -> TC LON down
rules.rationale: Exit (power) understeer, low corner speed: one less TC LON position (car_data.json tc table) permits more wheel spin under longitudinal load, reducing the diff-locking-driven understeer that power-on TC intervention can aggravate at low exit speed.

rules.name: Understeer, exit, medium speed -> rear ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Exit understeer, medium speed: stiffening rear ARB 1 position (both corners) lowers rear grip share relative to front, rotating the car more on exit and countering the understeer verdict.

rules.name: Understeer, exit, high speed -> rear ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Exit understeer, high speed: same rear-ARB-stiffer action as US-EXIT-med -- the decision matrix specifies an identical first change at this cell, not a larger step; only the speed-class binding differs.

rules.name: Oversteer, braking, low speed -> none
rules.rationale: No first-change action defined by the decision matrix for oversteer under braking at low corner speed -- recorded for 1:1 cell traceability, never fires.

rules.name: Oversteer, braking, medium speed -> rear ARB softer
rules.rationale: Rear-axle oversteer under trail-braking, medium speed: softening rear ARB 1 position lowers rear roll-stiffness share, freeing rear-axle grip under brake-release yaw.

rules.name: Oversteer, braking, high speed -> rear ARB softer
rules.rationale: Rear-axle oversteer under trail-braking, high speed: same rear-ARB-softer action as OS-BRK-med -- the decision matrix specifies an identical first change at this cell; only the speed-class binding differs.

rules.name: Oversteer, turn-in, low speed -> front toe toward zero
rules.rationale: Rear-axle oversteer at turn-in, low speed (mirror of US-TIN-low): reducing front toe-out by 0.5mm toward zero calms the sharpened turn-in rotation toe-out otherwise adds, working against the oversteer verdict at this phase.

rules.name: Oversteer, turn-in, medium speed -> diff position up
rules.rationale: Rear-axle oversteer at turn-in, medium speed (mirror of US-TIN-med): one more diff locking-torque position increases resistance to axle-speed difference on turn-in trail-throttle, stabilising the rear axle.

rules.name: Oversteer, turn-in, high speed -> wing up
rules.rationale: Rear-axle oversteer at turn-in, high speed (mirror of US-TIN-high): one wing step up adds rear downforce, directly countering aero-balance-driven rear instability at turn-in speed.

rules.name: Oversteer, apex, low speed -> front ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Sustained apex oversteer, low speed (mirror of US-APX-low). SITUATIONAL (matrix v2, project-lead review 2026-07-26): the matrix lists two valid levers here, grip-level dependent, and declines to pick one -- front ARB +1 (stiffening front roll-stiffness share, easing rear-axle load) OR rear ARB -1 (softening rear roll-stiffness share directly), depending on which axle is actually closer to its grip limit at the time. Always advisory: this is the engineer's judgment call, not an automatable first change.

rules.name: Oversteer, apex, medium speed -> diff position up
rules.rationale: Apex oversteer, medium speed, under partial throttle (mirror of US-APX-med). SITUATIONAL (matrix v2, project-lead review 2026-07-26): diff +1 (one more locking-torque position, stabilising the rear axle) OR clear the oversteer via toe/camber/ARB instead -- the matrix lists both without preference. Always advisory.

rules.name: Oversteer, apex, high speed -> front camber less negative
rules.rationale: Apex oversteer, high speed, sustained peak lateral load (mirror of US-APX-high). SITUATIONAL (matrix v2, project-lead review 2026-07-26): springs (platform-level stiffness change) OR rear ARB -1 OR front camber less negative (0.1deg, registry step corrected 2026-07-26) -- three valid levers, the matrix declines to pick one. Always advisory.

rules.name: Oversteer, exit, low speed -> TC LON up
rules.rationale: Exit oversteer, low speed: one more TC LON position permits less wheel spin under longitudinal load, directly reducing power-on rear-axle oversteer.

rules.name: Oversteer, exit, medium speed -> rear ARB softer
rules.rationale: Exit oversteer, medium speed: softening rear ARB 1 position lowers rear roll-stiffness share, freeing rear-axle grip on power application.

rules.name: Oversteer, exit, high speed -> wing up
rules.rationale: Exit oversteer, high speed, aero-dominated: one wing step up adds rear downforce and stability on power application at high exit speed.

rules.name: Instability, braking, low speed -> ABS rear-stable map
rules.rationale: Matrix v2 decode (project-lead review, 2026-07-26): the v1 literal ABS position-4 target (project-default) is replaced with the engineer's actual first change -- try-and-error 1-2 ABS positions within the current dry grip-level bracket, targeting the rear-axle-stable variant (car_data.json abs table). Ordinal nudge WITHIN a bracket, not a jump across grip levels -- see config/setup_parameters.json abs_position notes, 'superseded-in-practice' annotation, for the direction-semantics context this corrects. 1 chosen as the conservative default of the matrix's stated 1-2 range, per this project's existing convention (cf. the rake package magnitude).

rules.name: Instability, braking, medium speed -> rake reduction
rules.rationale: Destabilising yaw under braking, medium speed: 1mm of rake reduction (front ride height up, rear down -- WP2b-2 decision (1)) shifts the aero platform's pressure centre forward, calming the destabilising yaw moment while trail-braking. Opposite pairing from US-BRK-high's 'rake forward' package -- same two-parameter mechanism, reduction instead of addition.

rules.name: Instability, braking, high speed -> front toe more toe-out
rules.rationale: Destabilising yaw under braking, high corner speed: 0.5mm more front toe-out sharpens the front axle's response to counter-steer input while trail-braking, adding front-axle authority against the destabilising yaw moment. Elicitation fact (matrix v2, project-lead review 2026-07-26): rear toe-out is never run on this car -- front toe is the only axle this lever applies to.

rules.name: Instability, combined entry -> dropped
rules.rationale: Instability at combined entry (brake+turn-in) has no first-change action defined by the decision matrix -- deliberate scope drop, confirmed in WP2b-2 approval. INST-BRK (braking phase alone) is the only instability-scenario coverage in this ruleset; recorded here for 1:1 cell traceability, never fires.

_comment_elicitation_provenance: Provenance of each matrix-derived/held rule against the external decision matrix record, applied 2026-07-26 from the authoritative markup supplied for this ruleset: engineer-verbatim (12 elicited cells + 2 held escalations that inherit it -- a first-change lever the engineer stated directly, unmarked in the matrix), project-default (8 elicited cells, asterisked in the matrix -- a default this project chose absent a clean explicit engineer statement for that exact cell: US-BRK-low/garbled ABS answer, US-TIN-high/wing direction, US-APX-low/bare "ARB" defaulted to front, US-APX-high/camber step, OS-BRK-high/bare "rear ARB" presumed -1, OS-EXIT-med/sign-corrected from the engineer's stated "+1" (the S8-Med case), INST-BRK-low/ABS defaulted, INST-BRK-high/axle presumed front -- plus 1 held escalation, US-BRK-high-esc, whose bump-HS direction was also defaulted, not inherited from its verbatim base cell US-BRK-high), mirror-derived (6 cells marked "m" in the matrix -- OS-TIN-low/med/high, OS-APX-low/med/high -- structurally mirrored from the opposite-verdict cell's lever, not independently stated for this cell). null for dropped/retired rules (never fire, provenance moot). Policy (settings.action_class.cap_non_verbatim_to_advisory): a rule whose provenance is not engineer-verbatim is capped to ADVISORY regardless of severity/corroboration, UNTIL an engineer confirms that specific cell and its status is promoted to "reviewed" -- the cap is config-resident (can be switched off globally) but the INTENDED lift path is per-cell via status, not the global switch. Confirmation list for the engineer: exactly the 8 project-default + 6 mirror-derived cells (see PLAN.md engineer follow-up questions).
